content.text:
Quoted Content-Type parameter values are now parsed per RFC 9110. The full unit suite passes (2359 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped) and eslint is clean on the changed files.

**Behaviour**
- In `lib/content-type.js` I replaced the `;`-splitting regex with a small scanner.
- `multipart/mixed; boundary="part;one"; charset=utf-8` now gives `boundary=part;one` and `charset=utf-8`.
- `text/plain; title="lang=en; charset=latin1"` gives only `title`, with no `charset` parameter.

**Decisions to confirm**
- Backslash escapes inside quoted values are now unescaped (`\"` becomes `"`), and `toString()` re-escapes `"` and `\`. The old code did neither.
- An unterminated quote makes the parameter `invalid quoted string` and discards the rest of the header. Previously parsing resumed at the next `;`.

The new tests are in `test/content-type.test.js`; they cover both reported cases, escaped quotes with the `toString()` round trip, and the unterminated-quote case.
